description.narrative: IFC anticipates that the Project will contribute to narrow the finance gap for SMEs in Paraguay, supporting financial inclusion in the country. The SME finance gap in Paraguay is US$3.9 billion according to the SME Finance Forum, representing approximately 14% of the country's GDP. Informal micro and SME demand for finance is estimated at another US$3.6 billion. Improving access to finance and thus productivity of SMEs is crucial for the development of Paraguay's economy, as SMEs are a key driver of economic growth and job creation. Furthermore, 25% of the proceeds are expected to be used to originate loans to women-owned SME, a key underserved sub-segment in the economy. According to the World Bank Group MSME database, only 19% of SMEs are owned by women in Paraguay, and the vast majority of female-owned businesses are micro. Further, there is no well-defined women-owned SME-focused lending on the market. With its earmarked contribution of 25% for WSME lending and technical assistance to improve Banco Atlas capacity to expand and track WSME loans, IFC envisions contributing to the inclusiveness of the Paraguayan financial sector. By working with the fastest-growing SME bank in the country, IFC intends to demonstrate the financial viability of lending to WSMEs to other financial institutions while also increasing the competitive pressure in the financial sector.

The proposed investment consists of a 4-year IFC loan to Banco Atlas S.A. (Banco Atlas or the Bank) for up to US$50 million to expand the Banks small and medium enterprises (SMEs) lending program, of which at least 25% will be on-lent to Women-Owned SMEs (WSMEs) (the Project).
